security_assessment.conclusion: Default user off; role reset/default-deny; 256-bit fresh per-role credentials hashed in the ACL file. Literal validated fixture-key selectors, no wildcard key grants. Ledger mutations are confined by key kind to fixed run/job/rate/reservation keys; no authority-record writes. Six fixed source operations are the only loaded case operations. All 46 direct ledger authority probes are NOPERM with the same retained final-state hash.
security_assessment.qualification: The generated private ACL/credential material is intentionally discarded. The retained init ACL digest is not independently recomputable without inventing private inputs; validation relies on the source/image-bound runtime check plus actual denial receipts.

security_assessment.conclusion: Every clock invocation has exactly the observer credential, not ledger/setup/loader/boot/revoker credentials. Source-bound observer grants are read-only. The clock path AUTHs the fixed Unix socket and reads INFO SERVER and TIME; the host wait sleeps. Four actual clock envelopes bind to the same resumed server run, fixture, and rate-before hash, and each completes before its successor/after dispatch.
security_assessment.qualification: No separate runtime observer-write negative probes or command trace were retained. The 46 denials test the ledger identity, not the observer. No trace or additional Redis commands were run in this review.

security_assessment.conclusion: Four retained admission specs match exact images, fixture/case, closed entrypoints, image environment digests, finite memory limits and exact named-volume mounts. Executor/revoker have read-only control mounts and no data mount. Controller predicates enforce network=none, read-only rootfs, no privileged mode/binds/devices/ports/custom DNS, private IPC/PID mode, all capabilities dropped except init CHOWN, no-new-privileges, restart=no, bounded tmpfs/CPU/PIDs/memory. All ten unique retained runtime envelopes show exactly two processes, no external routes, loopback plus nine permitted down fallback devices, UID 65534/capabilities zero except init UID0/CHOWN. Redis listens only on the fixed mode0600 Unix socket, not TCP.
security_assessment.qualification: Raw Docker inspections and process argv inventories were not retained, only their digests, bounded specs and runtime assertions. These are source-bound observations, not continuous activity tracing or proof about a compromised host/daemon.

security_assessment.conclusion: Probe bytes/hash bind to the exact fixture and plan, survive the journaled kill/restart with a changed Redis run ID, and bind to resume/BOOT. All four clock receipts use the same new run ID. Before/after receipts hash-bind resume and the exact before/wait prefixes; measurement source rechecks INFO SERVER on entry. Init confirms empty volumes and the bound Redis config.
security_assessment.qualification: Two ready completions are journal-only. No raw ready envelope or per-command transcript is invented; neither discarded credentials nor owner/reservation IDs are reconstructed.

security_assessment.conclusion: Setup/loader/boot held sessions terminate and reconnects are denied before the measurement phases. Worker stop/wait/PID0/removal precedes creation of the fresh revocation helper. Final receipts cover all six roles with server_reachable=true and reconnect=denied: setup/loader/boot already_revoked, ledger/observer/revoker terminated. The source/recipe target tuple executes setup, loader, boot, ledger, observer, revoker, deleting revoker last. Held-session EOF/reset and fresh AUTH WRONGPASS are required, so a dead server cannot count as revocation. Redis remains until after revocation and helper removal.
security_assessment.qualification: JSON map order is not used as revocation-order proof. The ordered source/recipe loop plus actual completion receipt supplies that evidence; per-role timestamps are not exported.

security_assessment.conclusion: Case bound 300 seconds, command/stage 30 seconds, independent cleanup 60 seconds, controller elapsed 21736ms, observed post-worker cleanup 1363ms. Hard per-stage process alarm and worker removal prevent abandoned exec work from surviving teardown. Twenty maximum clock observations versus four observed, 128 action cap versus 33 observed, 2MiB artifact/combined-command-output limits, bounded RESP and snapshot reads. Retained container memory caps are 128MiB init, 256MiB executor/revoker, 528MiB Redis with 400MiB Redis maxmemory; tmpfs 16MiB, PIDs64, CPU1.
security_assessment.qualification: The run does not retain cgroup peak-memory telemetry. Earlier image-validation peaks are separately identified and are not misrepresented as this run's peaks.
